data.one_liner: Dart implementation of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for LLM applications.
data.what_it_does: Exposes data, tools, prompts, and resources to Large Language Model (LLM) applications through standardized protocols. Supports stdio, legacy SSE, and Streamable HTTP transports with built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization.
use_when: You need to build an MCP server in Dart to serve resources, tools, or prompts to LLMs.
Your Flutter or Dart backend needs to securely expose local functionality or data via stdio or HTTP transports.
avoid_when: You are just writing a standard REST or GraphQL API without LLM integration needs.
strengths: Supports every MCP protocol revision through 2026-07-28.
Includes multi-transport capabilities (stdio, SSE, Streamable HTTP).
Provides built-in JSON schema validation and OAuth 2.1 authorization.
weaknesses: Niche domain specific strictly to the Model Context Protocol.
Requires careful security and session management configuration when exposed over HTTP.
data.setup_notes: No special build steps or native permissions required; works wherever dart:io is available.
